input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign: vLLM ROCm serving functional and performance parity

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: whether vLLM serving on AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm) reaches functional and performance parity with the productized CUDA builds for the platform's supported model set. It runs a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware and produces the parity data plus a go/no-go recommendation that determines the scope of ROCm serving runtime productization.

## Scope

- Secure access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes — engaging procurement and/or partner labs (the securing work is in scope; the access being granted is an externally controlled precondition tracked as a risk, not an acceptance criterion).
- Define the campaign methodology before measurement begins: enumerate the supported model set, define functional pass/fail criteria per model, and define performance parity thresholds and the comparison baseline (the productized CUDA vLLM runtime on equivalent-class hardware, or a baseline recorded in the plan).
- Execute the campaign using upstream vLLM ROCm builds on the physical AMD Instinct nodes: functional correctness per model and performance measurement per model.
- Produce the go/no-go report: per-model functional and performance results, the list of models that clear both bars, and the recommended productization scope (full go / partial go / no-go).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written campaign plan exists that enumerates the supported model set, the functional pass/fail criteria, and the performance parity thresholds with the named comparison baseline, before measurement results are recorded.
- Functional results are recorded per model in the supported set as pass/fail against the plan's criteria.
- Performance results are recorded per model with the comparison baseline identified.
- A go/no-go report is produced that lists the cleared model set and states the recommended productization scope.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishing functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks / Notes

- Hardware availability is externally controlled (procurement or partner-lab queues); campaign start and turnaround depend on it. The report deliverable is the controllable completion point.
- Upstream ROCm image cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream communities; the campaign should pin and record the exact upstream build versions used so results are reproducible.

# Productize a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for campaign-cleared models

## Description

This epic delivers a supported, productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime for exactly the models the AMD Instinct validation campaign clears, shipped through the platform's existing serving stack so users can deploy those models on AMD Instinct nodes via InferenceServices.

## Scope

- Build a ROCm variant of the vLLM serving runtime image in the existing midstream repository, pinned to a specific, rebuildable upstream ROCm base image.
- Define the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime manifest exposing the ROCm vLLM runtime for the cleared model set, following the pattern of the existing productized runtimes.
- Validate end-to-end serving through KServe: InferenceServices using the ROCm runtime deploy and serve on AMD Instinct nodes (KServe itself requires no code change — it deploys ServingRuntime-based predictors generically — so this validation is an acceptance criterion here, on the owning team's epic).
- Release the runtime through the component's existing build pipeline as part of a platform version.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The vLLM ROCm runtime image builds and its build pipeline run is green in the component's existing pipeline.
- The runtime's upstream ROCm base image is pinned to a specific, rebuildable reference recorded with the build.
- A ServingRuntime exposing the ROCm vLLM runtime is defined for the cleared model set.
- An InferenceService using the ROCm runtime deploys on AMD Instinct nodes and its OpenAI-compatible endpoint successfully serves a cleared model.
- The runtime's supported model list matches the go/no-go scope produced by the validation campaign.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears.

## Risks / Notes

- Gated on the validation campaign outcome: if only a subset of models clears, scope narrows to that subset; if no model clears, this epic is removed and AMD serving productization is de-scoped.
- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream communities; alignment with platform release trains is outside our control. The pin-and-rebuild approach in scope is the mitigation; a cadence misalignment may delay which platform version carries the runtime but does not change the approach.

# PyTorch ROCm training support in the Training Operator (single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs)

## Description

This epic makes PyTorch training on AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm) a supported path for the Training Operator: PyTorchJobs running ROCm PyTorch images run correctly with AMD GPU resources, in both single-GPU and multi-GPU (multi-worker) job topologies, on clusters with AMD GPU-enabled worker nodes.

## Scope

- Enable PyTorchJob worker pods to run ROCm PyTorch training images with AMD GPU resource requests and the required device allocation on AMD Instinct nodes.
- Validate single-GPU PyTorchJob execution on ROCm to completion (loss converges / job succeeds).
- Validate multi-GPU, multi-worker PyTorchJob topologies on ROCm to completion, with AMD GPUs allocated per replica.
- Release the changes through the component's existing build pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using a ROCm PyTorch image runs to completion on an AMD Instinct node with the AMD GPU device correctly allocated to the worker.
- A multi-GPU, multi-worker PyTorchJob runs to completion on AMD Instinct nodes with AMD GPUs allocated per replica.
- The component's build pipeline run for these changes is green.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, shared with the Kueue quota epic): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs — this epic covers the Training Operator side (job execution on AMD GPUs); admission and amd.com/gpu quota handling are covered by the companion Distributed Workloads epic.

## Risks / Notes

- Requires access to AMD Instinct worker nodes for validation (externally controlled availability; tracked as a risk, not an acceptance criterion).
- PyTorch ROCm runtime images are published upstream; version choices are an implementation detail for the team, resolved when the work starts.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for ROCm training workloads

## Description

This epic makes the platform's queueing layer handle AMD GPU quota for ROCm training: workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu` resources are admitted through Kueue with correct quota accounting and all-or-nothing (gang) semantics, so single- and multi-GPU PyTorch training jobs on AMD Instinct nodes can be queued and admitted like their NVIDIA counterparts.

## Scope

- Support `amd.com/gpu` as a quota-accounted resource in the Kueue quota model (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue resource flavors), following the existing pattern for NVIDIA GPU quota.
- Validate admission of single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs requesting `amd.com/gpu`: all-or-nothing admission via waitForPodsReady for multi-replica jobs, correct pending behavior when quota is exhausted, and admission when quota frees up.
- Release the changes through the component's existing build pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A ClusterQueue configured with `amd.com/gpu` quota admits a PyTorchJob requesting AMD GPUs, with multi-replica jobs admitted all-or-nothing (waitForPodsReady gang semantics).
- A job requesting more `amd.com/gpu` than the configured quota remains pending and is admitted once quota is released.
- The component's build pipeline run for these changes is green.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, shared with the Training Operator epic): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling — this epic covers the Kueue admission/quota side; job execution on AMD GPUs is covered by the companion Training Operator epic.

## Risks / Notes

- Validation benefits from access to AMD Instinct worker nodes, but quota/admission behavior can be largely exercised with resource mocks; node availability is an externally controlled precondition, not an acceptance criterion.
- Runs in parallel with the Training Operator work — different repositories, no shared build artifact; the PyTorchJob-through-Kueue integration is an existing integration exercised by both epics' acceptance criteria.

# Document AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement: supported hardware, driver prerequisites, validated model list

## Description

This epic authors the user-facing documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement: what AMD hardware is supported, what driver prerequisites users must satisfy, which models are validated for vLLM ROCm serving, and how to run and queue PyTorch training on ROCm. It runs after the implementation work so the docs describe what was actually built and validated.

## Scope

- New documentation topics covering:
  - Supported AMD Instinct hardware for serving and training.
  - Driver and node prerequisites for AMD GPU worker nodes.
  - The validated model list for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, matching the validation campaign's cleared model set and the productized runtime's supported model list.
  - Running PyTorch training jobs on ROCm, including amd.com/gpu quota configuration through the queueing layer.
- Technically review all new content against the implemented behavior before publication.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the supported AMD hardware and the driver prerequisites for AMD GPU worker nodes.
- Published documentation lists the validated model set for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, consistent with the validated campaign results and the productized runtime.
- Published documentation describes how to submit single- and multi-GPU PyTorch ROCm training jobs and configure amd.com/gpu quota.
- All new content is technically reviewed against the implementation by the owning engineers, with review sign-off recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. (Epic priority is P1 via the docs-authoring priority exception: strategy priority `Major` maps to P1; docs epics are exempt from priority inheritance.)

## Risks / Notes

- Content depends on the validation campaign outcome: if the campaign clears only a subset of models (or none), the validated model list topic reflects that outcome; a no-go removes the serving-runtime topics and narrows the epic to training documentation plus findings.

### Conditional outcome handling (no branch files)

The campaign has bounded outcomes (≤3): full go, partial go (subset of the supported model set clears), no-go. All three change only the **scope or existence of a single downstream epic** (the productization epic), not which epics exist in the plan — partial go narrows its model set, no-go removes it. This is exactly the `gated_by` + `gate_failure_impact` mechanism, so no `-BRANCH-<letter>-` files are emitted; duplicating the productization epic per outcome would create two epics building the same runtime surface plus an artificial serialization between them.
